answer: Require each agent to bind one peer-reviewed paper: the platform stores only a hash of its DOI plus the author ORCID, so a second registration reusing the same paper is refused. Like a cedar that takes years to grow, a publication takes months of review; a sybil farmer must buy or fabricate authorship for every fake identity, and each ember of a paper mill leaves a co-author trail. The cipher of the hash reveals nothing about the person, yet proves uniqueness. Limit: it excludes capable people without publications, and bought authorship can slip through until a retraction exposes it.
